results.title: Portugal FIFA World Cup 2026 preview: Player to watch out for, tactics, predicted playing XI - Sportstar
highlights:
A sixth World Cup appearance. The last dance. Cristiano Ronaldo is the proud owner of a never-ending goal catalogue and a crammed trophy cabinet but the centrepiece is still missing. This will be the final chance for this generation’s greatest goal-scorer to crown his legacy with a World Cup triumph.
[...]
Portugal has always been an enigma at the global event. The nation has always been blessed with players of immense talent but they have always failed to be greater than the sum of their parts. That will be Roberto Martinez’s biggest task when he takes his team to the North American continent.
[...]
Portugal boasts of one of the best midfields in the tournament in the form of Bruno Fernandes, Vitinha and Joao Neves. Bernardo Silva, who plays a much deeper role for Manchester City, is often shifted to the right wing for his country and that could prove to be counterproductive considering that the side’s wingers haven’t had great seasons at club level. But, there is enough pace and trickery on the flanks to make a sizeable impact off the bench when required.
[...]
The Selecao das Quinas have been placed in Group K alongside Colombia, DR Congo and Uzbekistan. While passage out of the group stage is expected, the early knockout rounds have been the side’s Achilles heel for the last few tournaments and that is where the side will hope its talisman can show the way.
[...]
Bruno Fernandes: Manchester United’s midfield maestro has been at his playmaking best this year, breaking the Premier League record for most assists in a single season. If the players around him manage to convert the chances he creates, Portugal will stand a chance to go deep into the tournament.
[...]
You don’t often criticise a manager that has just guided a team to third place in a World Cup but Martinez’s stint with Belgium felt more like a missed opportunity with a golden generation rather than an achievement. The Spaniard did not look too impressive in the beginning of his stint with Portugal but a UEFA Nations League title in 2025 has given the country hope that he could be the man to break the duck.
